chunks: 421 - Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Ali, from Al-Sadan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him: 'Is there a fixed time for this matter (the reappearance) in which we may rest our bodies and reach it?' He replied: 'Yes, but you people divulged it, so Allah increased it (postponed it).'

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter, specifically referring to the reappearance (al-Zuhur) of the Imam.

ai.seo_question: Why was the time of the Imam's reappearance postponed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the Shia doctrine of 'Taqdim wa Ta'khir' (acceleration and delay) of the Imam's reappearance, illustrating how the actions of the companions directly influenced the timeline of the Occultation. It underscores the dynamic nature of divine decree, where human agency in preserving or revealing esoteric knowledge can alter the appointed time of the Mahdi's return.
